newsitem.title: UK: UK's Granada profits jump after Forte deal.
newsitem.headline: UK's Granada profits jump after Forte deal.

text.p: British television and hotels company Granada Group Plc on Wednesday announced that first half profit had jumped by a third as the benefits of its takeover of Forte last year fed through.
Granada is poised to expand its British commercial television (ITV) operations through a deal to acquire northern neighbour Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television.
Chairman Gerry Robinson told Reuters that the two boards had agreed on a price of 1175 pence per share for the 73 percent of Yorkshire which Granada does not already own.
That level would value Yorkshire at 710-720 million pounds ($1.2 billion), leaving Granada to pay some 525 million pounds to acquire full ownership.
Granada is one of the leading ITV companies, operating licences for north-west England and London Weekend Television.
An acquisition of Yorkshire would allow Granada to reach a vast tract of northern England, from Liverpool in the north-west to Newcastle in the north-east.

Robinson said the deal would enable Granada to sell the whole area to advertisers as a single unit within the regionalised ITV network. It would also give a further boost to Granada's production output as the growth in new channels multiplies demand for programmes.
Robinson said the profit figures vindicated Granada's 3.9 billion pound takeover of hotel and catering empire Forte in January 1996 after a bitter battle.
"Everything that was promised has been delivered - and a bit more. The disposal programme has delivered all the cash but from fewer asset sales," he said.
The trading performance from the hotels and restaurants acquired in the takeover improved by more than 50 percent on a like-for-like basis.

Granada's pre-tax profit excluding exceptional items climbed 33 percent to 243 million pounds in the 26 weeks to end March, just ahead of analysts' forecasts. The dividend was raised 10 percent to 4.66 pence per share.

Granada shares, which have risen in recent days, slipped 8p to 894.5p by 0920 GMT as the FTSE 100 index of leading shares fell from an opening peak. The company said second half trading had begun encouragingly.

Granada, which has sold off hotels and motorway service stations since the Forte deal, said it had raised 1.3 billion pounds in disposals over the past 18 months. It has cut debt by 860 million pounds to 2.655 billion.
It still plans to sell a number of luxury Exclusive hotels acquired from Forte. Robinson said the sale of its 68 percent stake in London's Savoy Hotel Group was also on the agenda.
